$comment: Shipped defaults. Override per user in ~/.claude/self-review/config.json (or $SELF_REVIEW_CONFIG): objects deep-merge, arrays replace.
$comment.coldRun: uncontained: angle X executes nothing unless it achieves FULL containment — sandbox-exec on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux — and the entry points come back UNVERIFIED rather than clean. Denying only the network (unshare -rn, when bubblewrap is absent) does not count: it leaves writes and reads unconfined, so a buggy entry point still reaches the real filesystem with your permissions. Set this true only on a host you know holds no credentials; it then buys the best containment available, not none. It is not in REPO_ADDITIVE, so a checked-in .self-review.json cannot set it.

impact.$comment: Blast radius (impact.mjs). stopWords/exclude/fullFor/docsFor are arrays: an override replaces the whole list.
impact.$comment.wire: Wire contracts (lib/wire.mjs): how much identity a string must carry before the loop searches the tree for it. minLiteralChars is the length one literal SEGMENT must reach (`users` in `/users/:id`), not the total across the path; lower finds more consumers and more noise.

tier.$comment: Tier rules (tier.mjs). riskPaths match the repo-relative path, riskContent only added lines; both are regex fragments joined with |.
tier.$comment.executable: executable: paths that are entry points but carry no shebang of their own — a shebang or the execute bit is detected from the file itself, so this list is only for what cannot declare itself — never an extension, since a `*.sh` glob also claims the sourced-only library sitting next to the script. executableExclude: trees whose entry points are fixtures rather than the product; a bare name like Dockerfile matches by basename at any depth, and a test corpus is full of them.
